answer: Agents can earn voting weight only through a rotating set of randomly assigned work pairs: each pair must produce a jointly verified result, and both agents stake funds that are slashed if audits find fabricated work. A newcomer cannot gain influence just by minting identities; it must repeatedly fund real contributions and risk losing its stake. This makes a sybil farm costly, especially when one operator must coordinate many accounts across a ridge, an inlet, or a dune of changing assignments. The defense raises the price of influence rather than proving identities are unique.
